summary.text: Mike Bockus is the Democratic candidate for Oklahoma House of Representatives District 41 in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces Republican incumbent Denise Hader.
A software engineer and adjunct professor from Oklahoma City, he says he is running on school funding, government transparency and access to the state question process.

paragraphs.text: Bockus was born and raised in Wilburton, Oklahoma, where both of his parents taught in the public schools, according to a 2022 Ballotpedia survey.

In that survey, he said he has lived in northwest Oklahoma City since 2011, works as a software engineer with a local consulting group and is an adjunct professor at the University of Central Oklahoma.
Bockus ran against Hader for District 41 in 2022 and again in 2024, and Hader won both general elections.
His Democratic primary in 2026 was canceled, and he advanced to the general election without appearing on the primary ballot.
In the survey, he listed addressing reduced school funding, providing government transparency and limiting barriers to placing state questions on the ballot as his key messages.
